A1.relation: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement

A2.relation: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority

A3.relation: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation

A6.relation: History, persistence and reconstruction of support

formation.explanation: Qualified support is gathered before a decision is formed. A candidate counts granted votes (or pre-vote grants) and only becomes leader when the count reaches quorumSize(); the leader then records each voter's acknowledged match index through commitment.match, and commitment.recalculate advances commitIndex only when the majority match index is at least commitment.startIndex, the first index created in the leader's own term, so entries of earlier terms are never committed on match indexes alone. Followers advance their own commit index only from the leader's LeaderCommitIndex bounded by their own last index.

context.explanation: The context that qualifies support and authority is the adopted term plus the known leader identity. Inbound AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot ignore older terms and adopt a strictly greater one by writing StableStore and dropping to Follower; accepted AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot then record the leader identity, which requestVote/requestPreVote use to refuse support while a different leader is known. A leader loses authority locally through checkLeaderLease when it cannot contact a quorum of voters within LeaderLeaseTimeout, and gains it at the target through TimeoutNow, which puts the target into Candidate with candidateFromLeadershipTransfer. The same term/leader update is additionally reachable from a NetworkTransport connection goroutine through the registered heartbeat callback.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the term and at the own-term replication rule. A durable vote record is only re-granted for the same (term, candidate) and is otherwise superseded once a greater term is adopted, so support gathered in term T cannot be consumed in term T+1; conversely an RPC whose term is older than the adopted term is ignored, so a deposed leader cannot re-establish authority. On the leader side, a follower's match index only becomes usable support after the leader has matched a quorum at or beyond commitment.startIndex, so pending work from an earlier term constrains what the new leader may commit; and leadership transfer explicitly requires the target's nextIndex to be past the leader's lastIndex before TimeoutNow, so an up-to-date support context is a precondition for moving authority. Because both lines read and write the same current-term context, an entry point that updates that context outside the main goroutine (the transport heartbeat callback) is the point where the connection is not obviously serialized.

open_details: The pre-vote grant path was read at the level needed for the context path; its interaction with a concurrently observed leader was not traced to completion.
Snapshot-driven log truncation was read at its call sites; the interaction with a MonotonicLogStore implementation is recorded as a deferred surface.

The verification path is no longer unread for the quorum question: obligation c-verify-leader-voter-quorum was confirmed with a served check, and the remaining questions there are the repair location and whether any consumer outside the module relies on the confirmation.
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships and their connection are explained from actual code: formation and advancement are grounded in the vote tally, the pre-vote round, commitment.match/recalculate and the startIndex own-term rule; context and authority are grounded in the term/state update, leader identity update, the leader lease step-down and TimeoutNow. The connection is sourced: votes are only re-granted for the same term, older-term RPCs are ignored, match indexes are only usable at or after startIndex, and a transfer requires the target to be caught up. Three mechanisms that earlier versions of this map left as unknowns are now recorded where they belong: the transport heartbeat callback performs its term, state and leader writes without being serialized with the main goroutine and publishes the term through a plain atomic store; a client future for VerifyLeader or a batched Apply carries no shutdown escape once a completed Shutdown has left the buffered request channels unprocessed; and the candidate's self-vote is written for the proposed term without comparing it with the vote record, so a published term that has dropped by one makes the next election propose a term that already holds a vote and overwrite it while the transfer exemption keeps the campaign from being filtered. The third links to the first: the overwritten record is the only barrier the vote path's exemption leaves, and with the dual leadership in place the commit line inherits the consequence - a leader can count a voter's position for a command that voter never stored, because the follower's acknowledgement compares terms and not contents - and the overlap did not persist in the prefix that observed it: the second leader stepped down inside the window, which the review attributed by exclusion to the leader's own lease check, so the lease question that raised has since been answered: with the peers reachable and in the leader's own term, an accepted configuration, including one applied through the reload API, can make the lease end a leadership that a quorum could still contact, which is recorded as a bounded-liveness obligation of its own. The counter-parts that bound each mechanism are recorded beside them (the fast path cannot append logs or advance the commit index; the default unbuffered applyCh always completes and the leader lease and the replication path cover term discovery; the vote-granting path still refuses a second different vote in one term and a leader refuses a transfer request whose vote it already recorded), so no core gap is claimed and the overview stays usable.

question.question: After a node installs a snapshot that carries state the source had committed and applied through index J, does the commit context the node publishes - Raft.CommitIndex(), which is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation - identify a commit point at least J, or can the node hold applied state at J while reporting a lower commit index?
question.importance: The published commit index is the value a server uses to implement the read-index optimisation described in the Raft paper, so a node that under-reports it cannot be used to derive a read index for the committed state it already holds, and any client or monitor that relates the reported commit point to the applied point sees applied state ahead of committed state. The state in question is not speculative: the snapshot payload is the source's committed and applied FSM state, and the receiving node adopts it wholesale. The consequence is a client-contract one rather than a safety one, but the value the node publishes is wrong for the whole window in which it holds that state without having heard an advertised commit index, and on the startup restore path it is wrong until a leader contacts the node at all.
participants: the source node that committed and snapshotted the state
the voter that installs the snapshot
a client reading the installing node's commit index or Stats
objects: raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot written by installSnapshot
the snapshot index carried by InstallSnapshotRequest.LastLogIndex
the commit_index and applied_index entries of Raft.Stats
contexts: a voter in the source's configuration that installs the snapshot by the module's own InstallSnapshot path
the prefix immediately after the install, before any later AppendEntries advertises a commit index
event_paths: source path: Apply commits and applies entries, Snapshot persists the FSM at the applied index and compacts the log

install path: the request carries the snapshot metadata, installSnapshot copies the payload into a new sink, restores it through the FSM, sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the requested index, truncates the log, and answers success
observation path: the receiver's commit index, applied index, last index and state are read through the public accessors

counterevidence: The map records the follower's commit index as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex), which describes the append path only and can be read as defining the published value as the last advertised commit index rather than as the committed state actually held.

The receiving node's FSM has the state either way, so an application that reads its own FSM rather than the published index is unaffected.
No in-repo consumer other than Stats was located for the value on a follower, so no internal mechanism was found that misbehaves because of it.
unknowns: whether the omission is deliberate, i.e. whether the library intends the follower's published commit index to be strictly the leader's last advertisement
which consumers outside the module rely on the value on a follower, which would raise the consequence

question.trigger_rationale: The installer restores the snapshot and then publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from req.LastLogIndex, truncates the log and answers success; the commit index is written only in the appendEntries commit branch, as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex), so a node whose commit index is still at its old (or zero) value keeps reporting it while already applying through the snapshot index. The source's own report of the same index as committed and applied is what makes the comparison unambiguous: within this prefix the receiver's last index becomes that index, so the requirement that the published value may not fall below it is exactly the comparison the check performs.

grounding.derivation: Raft.CommitIndex() is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation and returns raftState.commitIndex (s-api-commit-index). On a follower that state is otherwise advanced only in the appendEntries commit branch, which sets it to min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex) and applies through processLogs (s-raft-append-commit). takeSnapshot persists the FSM at an index the node has applied (s-snapshot-take), and the payload the installer adopts is the source's committed state. installSnapshot itself publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from req.LastLogIndex and truncates the log but never writes the commit index (s-raft-install-snapshot), so the node leaves the commit index below an index it has already established as applied. The obligation therefore requires the published value to be at least the snapshot index on this path.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any node that accepts an InstallSnapshotRequest from a leader whose snapshot covers committed state. The check exercises a voter of the source's configuration installing a snapshot produced by that source's own Snapshot API, with the receiver's timers long enough that nothing else changes it inside the prefix.

feedback.answered: The last-log report of a node that adopts a snapshot is a cached value that is not refreshed by the adoption, in both configurations that were executed. With the log left intact the node reported last index 43 while the cached last log stayed at the bootstrap entry, and with the receiving node configured to truncate at the snapshot index the same pair appeared, last index 43 and last snapshot index 43 beside a cached last log of index one and term one. So the apparent inconsistency is explained by two different quantities - the effective last index, which takes the greater of the cache and the snapshot, and the cached last log entry, which the install path publishes unchanged - and the second execution removes the possibility that the value was merely accurate about an untouched store.
remaining: The same cached-value question for the runtime install path is now explained for the two executed configurations; whether any consumer depends on the cached last-log report rather than the effective one was not investigated.
Whether the two names warrant a documentation change remains a presentation question rather than an obligation.

Repair locations for the eleven confirmed obligations are still open, no external consumer was exercised for the client-contract findings, the campaign path of a server without a vote is not fully read, the transfer path accepts a non-voter target and reported success with no leader established, and the deferred third-party-transport, MonotonicLogStore and nested-module surfaces remain unread.
feedback.rationale: This is a small completion of an explanation already on the record, drawn from an execution the run had already paid for, so it costs no new obligation and closes one ambiguity in the earlier negative: the cached last-log report is independent of whether the store was actually truncated. The run is at its time boundary, so nothing further is opened.
